DESIGN. Two provenance maps kept deliberately apart:
- paramLinks: the struct a CALLER passed into funcAddr:paramIdx.
- paramViews: the struct the CALLEE itself built from that parameter.
A merge always requires the callee's corroboration, so two unrelated callers passing objects into the same slot are NOT linked to each other unless the callee actually dereferences that parameter as a struct. A passthrough helper taking a void* therefore links nothing. Identity is published in both directions, so caller-then-callee and callee-then-caller give the same answer — this REDUCES the order-dependence noted on peek-a-bin-z0r for the provenance path (the shape path's first-match-wins scan is unchanged).

THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST is the gate, which goes beyond what I asked for and is the right call: numbering only happens for a VERIFIED frame-pointer prologue (push rbp / mov rbp, rsp, seeing through MSVC hot-patch padding). Under frame-pointer omission RBP is more often a callee-saved object pointer than a frame pointer, so [rbp+0x10] is frequently a STRUCT FIELD ACCESS rather than a parameter. Numbering those would have fed precisely the false struct merges this bead exists to prevent — it would have made provenance net harmful rather than useful. x64 SHADOW SPACE, which I asked to be checked because it is where an off-by-one would hide: the first slot [rbp+0x10] is the ABI home slot for the argument passed in RCX, not the first stack-only argument, so (offset - 0x10)/8 gives 0..3 for the home slots and 4 for the fifth argument at [rbp+0x30]. REGISTER vs STACK CONFLICT: I suggested preferring the register mapping; the agent chose the opposite and justified it, and it is right. RCX is volatile and routinely reused as scratch after being spilled to its home slot, so crediting later accesses through RCX to parameter 0 is the more dangerous reading. Width-sensitive operators (bitwise, shifts, / and %) are now redone in BigInt when the operand says 8 bytes. BigInt is CONFINED TO THE EVALUATION: IRConst.value is a number, so a result that will not round-trip through one is REFUSED rather than approximated. That refusal is the design point — an unfolded expression still says what the machine does, while a rounded constant silently does not and nothing downstream could tell.

Also fixed on the way: +, - and * take exact double arithmetic on the way IN but can leave the exactly-representable range on the way OUT, so the switch now declines to fold a result past 2^53 instead of printing a rounded constant. THE SUBTLE PART, worth reading before touching fold.ts again: knownWidth() deliberately IGNORES IRConst.size. That field records the image's MODE — 8 for every immediate in a 64-bit binary — not the width the instruction wrote. Consulting it would read 'eax & 0xffffffff' as a 64-bit operation and suppress a legitimate fold. Width comes from a register, deref, cast, or the widest operand of a binary; null means no evidence and is treated as not-64-bit, which keeps the change to the case that is demonstrably unsound rather than every case that cannot be proved sound.

ONE DELIBERATE WIDENING of the proposed design, and the reasoning is good: repair is routed PER

newly covers.
